blocks.text: Full-text search inverts the document → words relationship: for every term, store the list of documents (and positions) containing it — a **postings list**. A query for "red shoes" intersects the postings for `red` and `shoes`, then ranks the matches. Building that index is the job of an analysis pipeline that turns raw text into normalised terms.

items: **TF-IDF / BM25:** a term that appears often in this document but rarely across all documents is a strong signal. BM25 (the Lucene/Elasticsearch default) adds length normalisation and saturation.
**Field boosts:** a match in the title counts more than in the body.
**Business signals:** popularity, recency, rating, personalisation — often a second-stage learning-to-rank model over the top few hundred candidates.
**Two-stage retrieval:** cheap recall (BM25 / vector ANN) → expensive re-ranking on a small candidate set.

sections.title: How an Elasticsearch cluster serves a query

steps.label: fetch phase: full docs for winners

items: Indexing is **near-real-time**: new documents become searchable after a refresh (~1 s by default).
Search is not the source of truth — feed it from the primary DB via CDC/events, and be able to rebuild it.
Deep pagination (page 1,000) is expensive; use search_after cursors.

blocks.text: Autocomplete must answer within ~50–100 ms as the user types, so it's served from precomputed structures rather than full search queries. The classic structure is a **trie** of popular queries where each node caches its top-k completions, so a lookup is just walking the prefix.

items.title: Collect
items.text: Log search queries (and selections) in a stream.

items.title: Aggregate
items.text: Hourly/daily job counts queries with time decay and filters bad/offensive terms.

items.title: Build
items.text: Construct a trie (or a prefix → top-k table) with top-k completions stored per node.

items.title: Serve
items.text: Ship the structure to in-memory servers; cache the hottest prefixes at the edge / client.

items.title: Update
items.text: Swap in a new version atomically; add a small real-time layer for trending queries.

blocks.title: Tip
blocks.text: A simpler alternative that interviewers accept: store `prefix → [top 10 completions]` in Redis/KV for prefixes up to ~10 characters. It's just a big precomputed map.

items: Fuzzy matching via edit distance (Levenshtein automata) or n-gram indexes.
Synonym dictionaries (sneakers ↔ trainers) at query or index time.
Language-specific analysers; CJK languages need segmentation rather than whitespace tokenisation.
Spelling correction: "did you mean" from query logs.

blocks.title: Say it in the interview
blocks.text: I'd index products into Elasticsearch via CDC from the primary database, rank with BM25 plus popularity boosts and a re-ranking model, and serve autocomplete from a precomputed prefix → top-k map that's rebuilt hourly from query logs.
